recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Future authoritative SupplyRequest or SupplyDelivery wording changes should be made in HL7/oo-incubator; core follow-up is only needed if active core pages again imply SupplyRequest should merge with DeviceRequest or that SupplyRequest records patient-specific clinical use.
issue_request: FHIR-38897 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 Orders and Observations issue asking to maintain DeviceRequest and SupplyRequest as separate resources. DeviceRequest was to remain patient-specific clinical device use, while SupplyRequest was to remain logistics/movement of supplies, with deliverTo Patient used only as delivery destination context and SupplyDelivery tracking actual movement.
initial_application: The issue was applied before R5 publication through PR #2630. Merge commit 47fccfe6c1 listed FHIR-38897, and commit ac8c3aa2b3 added SupplyRequest narrative saying it is logistics-only, Patient in deliverTo is only a delivery destination and not clinical use, SupplyRequest expresses the need to deliver an item, SupplyDelivery tracks actual delivery, and RelatedPerson is allowed for deliverTo.
additional_context: FHIR-39066 later made the same SupplyRequest/DeviceRequest separation actionable by removing the remaining active workflow combination question and is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-39509, FHIR-39510, and FHIR-39511 are neighboring SupplyRequest updates already represented on the combined branch. Later core history intentionally moved SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery out of active core into HL7/oo-incubator, and active core pages link those resources externally.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current active core DeviceRequest remains patient-specific, the active workflow note has already been narrowed by FHIR-39066, source/fhir.ini no longer builds SupplyRequest or SupplyDelivery, and the OO Incubator SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery source contains the requested logistics, delivery-context, and movement-boundary language.
